evaluated.name: IndustryWCAccrualGrossProfit
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Within an industry, firms that grow gross profitability without inflating working capital convert operating strength into cash, while peers with similar margins but rising working-capital accruals are financing reported profit with receivables and inventory.
evaluated.reasoning: Balance-sheet working-capital accruals isolate the most manipulable component of income, and gross profitability is the cleanest, least-manipulated quality measure; both are heavily industry-dependent, so industry z-scoring makes the interaction comparable across business models. The joint rank targets cash-validated profitability rather than either effect alone.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OperatingCycleAccrualMarginTrend
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(recch, ADD(invch, apalch)), at), TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: The receivable, inventory and payable components of the cash flow statement are the most discretionary and least verifiable part of accruals; firms that release cash from the operating cycle while their gross margin is genuinely trending upward are converting real competitive improvement into cash, unlike firms whose margin gains sit in receivables and inventory.
evaluated.reasoning: Cash-flow-statement components (recch, invch, apalch enter oancf with a positive-equals-cash-inflow convention) isolate the operating cycle directly rather than inferring it from noisy balance-sheet differences that are contaminated by mergers and reclassifications. Pairing this with a five-year gross-margin trend separates durable pricing/cost improvement from margin that was manufactured through channel stuffing or inventory build.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConservativeAccrualStreakMargin
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1)), 0), 5), MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 3))
evaluated.hypothesis: A single year of negative accruals can be a timing artifact, but a multi-year streak of shrinking non-cash working capital reveals a habitual conservative reporting and tight operating-capital regime; combined with a high sustained gross margin, this identifies firms whose profitability is structurally cash-generating.
evaluated.reasoning: Counting how many of the last five years had negative working-capital accruals converts a noisy annual flow into a persistence state, which is the concept the economic story actually requires and which no level-based accrual measure captures. The margin leg ensures the streak reflects disciplined cash conversion of a profitable business rather than a firm liquidating working capital while its economics deteriorate.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WorkingCapitalIntensityDrift
evaluated.expression: NEG(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), sale), 1), 1))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is not the dollar accrual but whether non-cash working capital is expanding faster than the revenue base that justifies it; a rising working-capital-per-dollar-of-sales ratio means receivables and inventory are being built without commensurate demand, and that gap reverses into future earnings and returns.
evaluated.reasoning: Benchmarking the accrual stock against contemporaneous revenue makes this a revenue-conditioned accrual measure rather than the asset-deflated Sloan variable, so a firm can have large positive accruals and still score well if sales grew proportionally — the ranking is not a monotone re-parameterization of total accruals. Sales is almost always strictly positive, so the deflator is numerically stable, and I have dropped the earnings-stability gate entirely because the critic is right that the accrual anomaly is not concentrated in low-volatility firms.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: DepreciationConservatismProfitability
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(dpc, sale)), MA(RATIO(ni, ceq), 3))
evaluated.hypothesis: Depreciation is the largest non-discretionary-looking but in fact highly discretionary accrual; within an industry, firms charging more depreciation per dollar of sales are reporting conservatively, so when such a firm still shows high sustained ROE its cash earnings power is understated rather than inflated.
evaluated.reasoning: I abandoned the taxes-payable channel because the critic is correct that Δtxp is a current-liability increase that mechanically *reduces* accruals — the sign in my original was backwards — and because txp is sparsely populated and economically trivial relative to assets. The depreciation-policy channel keeps the same "is reported profit validated by conservative accounting?" mechanism using dpc, which is well populated on the cash flow statement, and industry z-scoring removes the capital-intensity confound so the leg measures policy conservatism rather than asset mix.

evaluated.name: AccrualPenaltyAtLowProfitability
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 3), MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 1))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 3)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A given working-capital build is far more dangerous for a firm with a thin profit base, which cannot absorb the eventual write-down, than for a highly profitable firm whose cash generation easily covers it; the accrual penalty should therefore steepen as sustained gross profitability falls.
evaluated.reasoning: The unstable gross-profit denominator is replaced by a bounded [0,1] gate, RANK(NEG(smoothed gross profitability)), multiplying an asset-deflated, winsorized accrual z-score, so there is no sign flip or explosion when gross profit is small or negative — the structural defect the critic identified is removed while the economic claim survives intact. The first SUMRANK channel retains the gross-profitability main effect so that high-quality firms are not shrunk into the neutral middle by the gate, giving a monotone quality tilt plus a quality-conditional accrual slope.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: RetainedEarningsCashGap
evaluated.expression: NEG(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(re, 1), at), RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at)), 1))
evaluated.hypothesis: Retained earnings growth records what management says it earned and kept; the change in the cash balance records what actually arrived. When retained earnings rise year after year without any corresponding cash accumulation, the reported profit was absorbed by soft accruals and unproductive investment, and subsequent returns are poor.
evaluated.reasoning: This drops the leverage leg the critic correctly identified as the net-debt-issuance anomaly and replaces it with a direct book-versus-cash reconciliation that no financing or accrual factor in the archive measures: it compares the stock of claimed cumulative profit to the stock of realized cash. Both legs are deflated by total assets rather than by book equity, so negative or near-zero equity cannot generate sign-flipped extremes, and the winsorization only trims genuine outliers rather than repairing a structural defect.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualWithEarningsStability
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at))), NEG(VOL(RATIO(ni, ceq), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The task's core story is that low accruals plus stable earnings identify genuinely cash-backed performance; stable ROE means the earnings level is a persistent state, so a low accrual attached to it is credible evidence of repeatable cash generation rather than a transitory swing in the operating cycle.
evaluated.reasoning: Every strong archive result so far uses gross profitability as the quality leg, leaving the literal earnings-persistence dimension untested against the industry-neutralized accrual leg — this fills that gap and tells us whether the quality channel that matters is profit *level* or profit *stability*. The five-year ROE volatility window will reduce coverage somewhat, which is the diagnostic cost of the test and is why I run it alongside, not instead of, the profitability-leg variants.

evaluated.name: AccrualPenaltyAtHighLeverage
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 1))), RANK(RATIO(lt, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual build must eventually be financed; a highly levered firm cannot carry an inflating receivable and inventory position without a funding or covenant problem, so the reversal of accruals is faster and more damaging when the balance sheet is already stretched.
evaluated.reasoning: The prior conditional signal (accrual penalty amplified at low profitability) delivered fmb 4.53 and 5.2% alpha, so the conditional architecture works; this changes the conditioning variable to leverage, which is nearly orthogonal to gross margin and captures the financing-capacity mechanism instead of the profit-cushion mechanism. The gate is a bounded [0,1] rank and the accrual leg is asset-deflated and winsorized, so there are no denominator sign flips, and the gross-profitability main effect is retained in the first channel.

evaluated.name: WeakestLinkCashQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable cash earnings require both conditions simultaneously — real operating profitability and no accrual inflation — so a firm should be judged by its weaker dimension: high margins financed by a receivable build are not cash-backed, and clean accruals at a firm with no gross profit are not earnings at all.
evaluated.reasoning: Taking the minimum of two industry-standardized legs is a conjunctive, non-additive operator: unlike SUMRANK or the numerator subtraction of cash-based operating profitability, it refuses to let a strong profitability score compensate for an aggressive accrual, which is exactly the economic claim the task makes and is not what any published cash-profitability measure computes. It uses the same well-covered balance-sheet inputs as the archive leader, so any difference in performance is attributable purely to the conjunctive versus compensatory aggregation rule.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: WorkingCapitalBloatVsPeers
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), sale))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The informative quantity is the accumulated stock of non-cash working capital a firm carries per dollar of sales relative to its industry peers, not this year's flow: persistent bloat means receivables and inventory that peers with the same business model do not need, which eventually becomes write-offs and margin pressure.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the smoothing-horizon tweak the critic rejected and switches from a flow to a stock construct, which is a different economic mechanism: balance-sheet bloat and stale operating assets rather than the annual accrual that must reverse next year. Deflating by sales and industry-standardizing makes the level comparable across operating cycles, and pairing it with industry-relative gross profitability asks whether the bloat is being carried by a genuinely profitable franchise or is masking deteriorating economics.

evaluated.name: AccrualInnovationVsOwnRegime
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), MA(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 5)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms have permanently different normal accrual levels because of their operating cycle, so the reversal-prone quantity is the deviation of this year's accrual from the firm's own multi-year norm; a profitable firm whose accruals suddenly jump above its own regime is the clearest manipulation candidate.
evaluated.reasoning: The critic is right that TS_RANK over five annual points yields at most five values and reproduces the lumpy-tie problem, so the firm-relative concept is now implemented as a continuous demeaning — current accrual minus its own five-year moving average — which preserves the within-firm interpretation with no ties at all. Winsorization controls the innovation tail, and the industry-relative gross-profitability leg supplies the quality dimension that distinguishes an accrual jump at a healthy franchise from routine noise at a marginal firm.

evaluated.name: AsymmetricAccrualBuildPenalty
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), NEG(MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 1), INDICATOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 0))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The accrual anomaly is asymmetric: positive accruals are discretionary builds of receivables and inventory that must reverse, while negative accruals often reflect distress-driven liquidation of working capital rather than superior cash conversion, so only the build side should be penalized.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the redundant level-plus-change construction with a genuine functional-form test — whether the accrual-return relation is one-sided — which no signal in the archive has examined and which speaks directly to distinguishing cash-backed performance from forced deleveraging. Firms with negative accruals receive zero in the penalty leg, but the continuous industry-relative gross-profitability leg breaks those ties, so the sort stays smooth and the portfolio composition stable.

evaluated.name: AccrualBuildWithoutDemand
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 1))), RANK(NEG(GROWTH(sale, 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A working-capital build is benign when it funds genuine revenue expansion — a growing firm must carry more receivables and inventory — but malignant when sales are flat or falling, because then it reflects unsold inventory, channel stuffing, or receivables the firm cannot collect.
evaluated.reasoning: Both prior conditional gates (low profitability, high leverage) delivered fmb above 4.5, so the architecture is validated; this substitutes demand growth as the gate, which is the economically correct scaler for working capital and is close to orthogonal to both the profit cushion and the balance-sheet constraint already tested. It should sharpen the short leg specifically by separating growth-driven accruals from stagnation-driven accruals, a distinction no archive signal makes.

evaluated.name: AccrualBuildWithMarginErosion
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at))), DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 1))
evaluated.hypothesis: Rising working capital combined with a deteriorating gross margin is the classic manipulation pattern — the firm is buying revenue with looser credit terms and discounting while capitalizing the cost in inventory — whereas a lean balance sheet with widening margins reflects real pricing power converted to cash.
evaluated.reasoning: Every strong archive result uses the *level* of profitability as the quality leg, so the direction of profitability has never been tested against the accrual leg; margin change is nearly orthogonal to margin level and captures the deterioration that makes an accrual build dangerous. Using a one-year margin change on well-covered income-statement items avoids the coverage collapse that destroyed the five-year cash-flow-statement trend signal.

evaluated.name: AccrualWithRetainedProfitHistory
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(re, at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Retained earnings relative to assets is the cumulative record of profits a firm has actually earned and kept over its whole life, an inherently persistent quality measure; a clean current accrual attached to a long history of retained profit identifies established cash generators, whereas clean accruals at a firm with a depleted retained-earnings base reflect a fragile, unproven business.
evaluated.reasoning: The quality leg in this archive has only ever been contemporaneous profitability or short-window earnings volatility, both of which are one- to five-year measures; retained earnings capture profit persistence over decades and are known to relate to firm maturity and payout capacity, giving a genuinely different quality dimension to interact with the accrual. It also uses only well-populated fields, so coverage should be at least as high as the 0.121–0.130 range seen for the re- and che-based signals.

evaluated.name: WorkingCapitalSlackVsOwnBest
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(SUB(RATIO(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), sale), TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), sale), 5))), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Every firm has demonstrated, at some point in the recent past, how leanly it can run its operating cycle; the gap between today's working capital per dollar of sales and that self-demonstrated minimum measures accumulated operating slack — uncollected receivables and unsold inventory the firm has proven it does not need — and that slack must eventually be written down.
evaluated.reasoning: This is neither the archived flow accrual nor the archived peer-relative bloat level: the benchmark is the firm's own five-year best operating efficiency, so permanent business-model differences in working-capital intensity are differenced out without imposing an industry classification, and a firm can look bloated versus peers yet clean versus its own attainable frontier. The distance-from-own-extreme construction is continuous, avoiding the tie problem of the streak signal, and pairing it with industry-relative gross profitability asks whether the slack sits at a franchise strong enough to absorb the write-down.

evaluated.name: AccrualPenaltyAtHighProfitability
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 1))), RANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Mispricing from accruals is largest exactly where investors have the most reason to extrapolate — highly profitable firms whose visible margins the market capitalizes eagerly; when such a firm's profit is not cash-backed, the disappointment is severe, whereas low-profit firms are already priced for bad news so their accruals carry less surprise.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's low-profitability gate (fmb 4.53, alpha 5.2%) assumed the accrual penalty is largest where the profit cushion is thin; this proposal reverses the conditioning direction on identical inputs, so the pair jointly identifies which side of the profitability distribution the accrual anomaly actually lives on — a substantive economic question, not a re-blend of archived legs. It abandons the MIN aggregation the critic correctly judged exhausted and keeps a continuous bounded gate plus the profitability main effect so the sort stays smooth.

evaluated.name: SupplierStretchAsNegativeQuality
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, wcap), dlc), 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Standard accrual measures treat a build in non-debt current liabilities as a good thing because it mechanically reduces accruals, but a ballooning payables balance is usually a firm financing itself by stretching suppliers under liquidity pressure, so the liability side should enter with the opposite sign from the Sloan convention.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than deleting the liability term as the critic rightly called a minimal edit, this flips its sign and tests it as a standalone quality channel against industry-relative profitability: the claim is that payables growth is a distress and supplier-financing signal, not an earnings-quality improvement. Because every archive accrual leg nets this term in with a positive earnings-quality interpretation, a positive result here would imply that all existing composites are mixing two opposite-signed economic forces inside one variable.

evaluated.name: WorstYearAccrualAggression
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(NEG(TS_MAX(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 5)), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accounting aggressiveness is a management trait revealed at its extreme, not on average: a firm that has posted one enormous working-capital build in the last five years has demonstrated a willingness to inflate reported performance, and that latent tendency contaminates its current earnings even in a year when accruals look clean.
evaluated.reasoning: Every temporal accrual construct in the archive uses a central tendency — one-year flow, five-year mean deviation, moving average, or a streak count — so the tail of the firm's own accrual distribution is untested, and it is precisely the tail that identifies discretionary reporting behavior versus routine operating-cycle variation. The measure is continuous (unlike the streak, whose Sharpe was 0.206) and pairs with the proven gross-profitability anchor, so a strong result would establish accounting-behavior extremity as a new state variable.

evaluated.name: AccrualBuildDrainingCash
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), NEG(MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 1), RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), at))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A working-capital build funded out of a shrinking cash balance is qualitatively different from one accompanied by rising cash: the first means reported profit is being consumed by the operating cycle and liquidity is deteriorating, the second means the firm is generating enough cash to fund growth and still accumulate reserves.
evaluated.reasoning: The gates tested so far are balance-sheet stocks (leverage) or income-statement flows (sales growth, margin); the direction of the cash balance is a distinct, directly observable verification of whether accruals were actually financed internally, and it is the one variable that adjudicates the task's central question of cash-backed versus paper performance. Unlike the failed retained-earnings-versus-cash gap, cash change enters here only as a bounded conditioning rank on the accrual, so it cannot invert the sort the way that standalone difference did.

evaluated.name: ProfitFloorWithCleanAccruals
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable earnings power is best measured by the worst year a firm has endured: a five-year minimum of gross profitability is the floor the business defends through downturns, and clean accruals attached to a high floor identify performance that is both cash-backed and cyclically robust.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive tested profitability as a level (strong) and as five-year ROE volatility (weak, alpha 2.7%), but never as a downside floor, which is the concept the "persistent, stable earnings" story actually requires and which discards the upside variation that makes a volatility measure penalize good firms. It is continuous, uses the same well-covered income-statement inputs, and if it outperforms the plain level anchor it redirects the remaining generations toward downside-persistence quality rather than contemporaneous profitability.

evaluated.name: CumulativeProfitAbsorbedByWorkingCapital
evaluated.expression: NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), LAG(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 5)), TS_SUM(SUB(revt, cogs), 5)), 1))
evaluated.hypothesis: Over a full business cycle, the fraction of cumulative gross profit that has been swallowed by an expanding operating cycle measures how much of a firm's reported profitability was never available as cash; a firm that consumed most of five years of gross profit financing receivables and inventory has been reporting profit it never collected.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not a concatenation of archived legs: accruals and profitability enter as a single economic quantity — cumulative working-capital expansion expressed as a share of cumulative gross profit — so the interaction is imposed by the accounting identity rather than by averaging two ranks. The denominator is a five-year sum of gross profit, which is large and almost always positive, curing the small-and-sign-flipping denominator problem that sank the earlier per-gross-profit ratio, and the five-year horizon distinguishes structural cash absorption from a single year's timing.

evaluated.name: CapitalEfficiencyWithCleanAccruals
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(sale, at)), NEG(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The DuPont decomposition splits profitability into margin and asset turnover, and it is turnover — the speed at which a firm converts its asset base into revenue — that is economically inseparable from accrual quality, because a fast-turning firm collects and sells before it must fund the operating cycle, whereas a slow-turning firm's reported profits are structurally locked up in working capital.
evaluated.reasoning: Every archive composite has anchored on the margin branch of DuPont, so the turnover branch is an untested and economically prior quality dimension: it speaks directly to whether reported earnings can be converted to cash, which is the task's question, rather than to how much profit is earned per sale. Because turnover and gross profitability are close to negatively correlated across industries, industry standardization is essential and included, and a strong result here would show the accrual effect certifies operating speed rather than pricing power.

evaluated.name: RepeatedAccrualBuildPenalty
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), NEG(MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 1), INDICATOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), LAG(at, 1)), 0))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A single year's working-capital build is usually operating noise that reverses on its own, but a build that follows another build is a ratchet — receivables and inventory that failed to convert last year and were added to again — and it is this repeated, unreversed accumulation that predicts write-downs and earnings disappointment.
evaluated.reasoning: The archived asymmetric penalty conditions only on the contemporaneous sign of the accrual, so the dynamic question of whether accruals reverse or ratchet across years is untested, and it is exactly the distinction between transitory accounting noise and durable balance-sheet deterioration that the task asks us to make. The conditioning term uses the prior-period asset base to detect whether the accrual was also positive a year earlier, the penalty magnitude stays continuous and winsorized, and the gross-profitability anchor breaks ties among the firms whose penalty term is switched off.

evaluated.name: AccrualBuildWhileLosingShare
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(SUB(wcap, che), dlc), 1), at), 1))), RANK(NEG(IND_ZSCORE(GROWTH(sale, 1))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What makes an accrual build suspicious is not slow growth per se but slow growth *relative to the firm's industry*: a firm whose revenue lags its peers while its receivables and inventory swell is losing share and propping up reported sales with credit terms and channel stuffing, whereas slow growth in a cyclically depressed industry is shared adversity, not manipulation.

evaluated.hypothesis: A given increment of working capital is far more likely to be uncollectible or obsolete at a firm that already carries a long operating cycle, because such a firm has demonstrated it cannot convert inventory and receivables quickly; adding to an already slow cycle compounds conversion risk, while the same build at a fast-turning firm clears within months.

evaluated.hypothesis: When non-cash current assets grow faster than the cost of goods actually sold, the firm is producing or purchasing ahead of demand — the classic real-earnings-management move that spreads fixed overhead across more units and flatters reported margins while burying the cost in inventory that must later be written down.
